text.p: Butler Manufacturing Co said Wednesday its backlog at the end of the third quarter was $329 million, up 17 percent from a year ago.
The increase was primarily due to higher margin products, as construction backlog was essentially flat, the building systems and specialty components company said.

"Butler's construction subsidiary continued to operate at lower than normal levels of earnings in the third quarter," Robert West, chairman and chief executive, said in a news release. "Actions are being taken to restore profitability to more acceptable levels."

The company also said that in recent weeks it repurchased about 73,000 shares of Butler stock at an average price per share of about $27.50 and the company said it intends to continue to use financial strategies that, along with its operating strategies, will increase Butler shareholder value.
"Prospects are good for a strong final quarter for 1996, and we believe we are well positioned looking ahead to the early months of 1997," West said.
Earlier, the company reported net income of $8.8 million, or $1.14 a share for the third quarter, compared to $7.7 million, or $1.00 a share a year ago.
